statement: The matrix calculus gradient (derivative) of the scalar trace function f(X) = tr(A X B X^⊤ C) with respect to matrix X is given in numerator layout by ∂tr(A X B X^⊤ C)/∂X = B^⊤ X^⊤ A^⊤ C^⊤ + B X^⊤ C A, and in denominator layout by ∂tr(A X B X^⊤ C)/∂X = C A X B + A^⊤ C^⊤ X B^⊤.

symbols.meaning: Matrix variable with respect to which the derivative is evaluated
Constant coefficient matrix compatible with X
Constant coefficient matrix compatible with X^⊤
Constant coefficient matrix completing the square matrix product
Trace operator summing diagonal elements of a square matrix

steps.text: Apply the cyclic permutation property of the trace to rearrange the matrix product inside the differential: d tr(A X B X^⊤ C) = d tr(C A X B X^⊤).
Commute the differential operator with the trace operator using trace linearity: d tr(C A X B X^⊤) = tr(d(C A X B X^⊤)).
Apply the product rule for matrix differentials to partition the product (C A X)(B X^⊤): tr(d(C A X B X^⊤)) = tr(C A X d(B X^⊤) + d(C A X) B X^⊤).
Distribute the trace over the sum by linearity: tr(C A X d(B X^⊤) + d(C A X) B X^⊤) = tr(C A X d(B X^⊤)) + tr(d(C A X) B X^⊤).
Factor out constant matrices from differentials (d(C A X) = C A (dX) and d(B X^⊤) = B d(X^⊤)): tr(C A X d(B X^⊤)) + tr(d(C A X) B X^⊤) = tr(C A X B d(X^⊤)) + tr(C A (dX) B X^⊤).
Apply the property that the differential of a transpose equals the transpose of the differential, d(X^⊤) = (dX)^⊤: tr(C A X B d(X^⊤)) + tr(C A (dX) B X^⊤) = tr(C A X B (dX)^⊤) + tr(C A (dX) B X^⊤).
Use the invariance of the trace under transpose (tr(M) = tr(M^⊤)) on the first term: tr(C A X B (dX)^⊤) + tr(C A (dX) B X^⊤) = tr((C A X B (dX)^⊤)^⊤) + tr(C A (dX) B X^⊤).
Apply the transpose-of-a-product identity to expand (C A X B (dX)^⊤)^⊤: tr((C A X B (dX)^⊤)^⊤) + tr(C A (dX) B X^⊤) = tr((dX) B^⊤ X^⊤ A^⊤ C^⊤) + tr(C A (dX) B X^⊤).
Cyclically permute terms under each trace so that dX is positioned on the right: tr((dX) B^⊤ X^⊤ A^⊤ C^⊤) + tr(C A (dX) B X^⊤) = tr(B^⊤ X^⊤ A^⊤ C^⊤ (dX)) + tr(B X^⊤ C A (dX)).
Combine terms by linearity of the trace and factor out dX: tr(B^⊤ X^⊤ A^⊤ C^⊤ (dX)) + tr(B X^⊤ C A (dX)) = tr((B^⊤ X^⊤ A^⊤ C^⊤ + B X^⊤ C A) dX).
Express the coefficient in transposed form for denominator layout conversion: tr((B^⊤ X^⊤ A^⊤ C^⊤ + B X^⊤ C A) dX) = tr((C A X B + A^⊤ C^⊤ X B^⊤)^⊤ dX).

Convert from differential form to derivative form: the coefficient of dX in tr(G dX) gives ∂tr(A X B X^⊤ C)/∂X = B^⊤ X^⊤ A^⊤ C^⊤ + B X^⊤ C A in numerator layout, while writing as tr(H^⊤ dX) gives ∂tr(A X B X^⊤ C)/∂X = C A X B + A^⊤ C^⊤ X B^⊤ in denominator layout.

assumptions.assumption: Matrices A, X, B, and C have compatible dimensions such that A X B X^⊤ C is square.
assumptions.breaks_when: Inner dimensions mismatch for matrix multiplication or the overall product is non-square, making the trace undefined.

assumptions.assumption: Matrices A, B, and C are constant with respect to X (dA = 0, dB = 0, dC = 0).
assumptions.breaks_when: A, B, or C depend on X, which would introduce additional differential terms.

assumptions.assumption: A specific layout convention (numerator vs. denominator layout) is adopted consistently.
assumptions.breaks_when: Numerator and denominator layout conventions are mixed without transposing to maintain compatibility.

failure_modes.signature: Transposed gradient matrices or dimension mismatches when combining matrix calculus identities.
failure_modes.cause: Confusing numerator layout (derivative of scalar with respect to matrix yields dimensions matching the transpose of denominator layout) with denominator layout.

failure_modes.signature: Matrix dimension incompatibility during trace manipulations.
failure_modes.cause: Cyclically shifting matrix factors within trace when individual factor products are non-square or dimensions do not align.
